title: LLM-Augmented Bayesian Optimization with Adaptive Policies for Chiplet Design Space Exploration
shortTitle: LLM-Augmented Bayesian Optimization with Adaptive Policies for Chiplet Design Space Exploration
abstract: Chiplet technology is a key approach for extending Moore's Law. However, its design process is constrained by two primary challenges: the scarcity of early-stage platforms for rapidly evaluating chiplet-based heterogeneous systems, and the complex relationships between design parameters and optimization metrics. To address these challenges, we propose a synergistic framework that integrates a Large Language Model (LLM) with Bayesian Optimization (BO), enabling architectural-level simulation and automated optimization for the 2.5D/3D CPU-GPU heterogeneous chiplets. We extend the open-source chiplet simulator to evaluate 3D designs by supporting graph topologies. Further, to enhance the exploration efficiency of BO, we introduce an LLM that generates high-quality policies to guide the optimization process, enabled by our proposed adaptive directional policy reasoning (ADPR) and an exploration gain-aware fine-tuning method. Finally, we use the policy-guided BO to perform an automated and efficient exploration of the complex chiplet design space. Experiments on 2.5D and 3D chiplet reveal that our framework improves design space exploration efficiency.

title: From Rainfall to Road-Network Functionality: Transferable Graph Forecasting for Flood-Disrupted Transportation Networks
shortTitle: From Rainfall to Road-Network Functionality: Transferable Graph Forecasting for Flood-Disrupted Transportation Networks
abstract: Extreme rainfall can rapidly degrade road-network functionality (RNF), disrupting emergency mobility, accessibility, evacuation, logistics, and infrastructure restoration. Existing flood-transportation impact models are often difficult to deploy across regions because they rely on local calibration, intensive simulation workflows or target-region retraining. This study proposes G-R2R, a transferable spatiotemporal graph-learning framework that reframes rainfall-induced road-network disruption as a region-conditioned, topology-flexible graph forecasting problem for unseen transportation networks. The framework integrates ego-centered subgraph sampling, terrain-conditioned graph representation, region-conditioned dual-level static encoding, and dynamic rainfall-network feature learning. Static geographic and infrastructure attributes are fused with rainfall forcing and recent RNF states to forecast node-level RNF across heterogeneous road networks. G-R2R is evaluated using simulation-derived RNF sequences from ten flood-prone regions in Wenzhou, China, under unseen-region testing protocols. It outperforms representative forecasting baselines, achieving a stabilized MAPE of 2.33% and $R^2$ of 0.855 under the fixed unseen-region benchmark. Leave-one-area-out evaluation yields stabilized MAPE values of 2.30%-3.54%. Ablation analysis supports the contributions of the terrain-conditioned graph representation and dual-level static encoding. A historical-event replay of Typhoon Fitow further shows that G-R2R reproduces principal temporal trajectories and node-level spatial patterns of the simulation-derived RNF reference under observed rainfall forcing without target-region retraining. These results support rapid and transferable node-level RNF forecasting across the regional road-network domains represented in this study.

title: EarthAlign: Learning Language-Aligned Representations of Earth System Data
shortTitle: EarthAlign: Learning Language-Aligned Representations of Earth System Data
abstract: Interpreting Earth system conditions is central to understanding environmental risks and informing decisions across weather- and climate-sensitive sectors. Existing multimodal weather systems primarily target task-specific prediction, generation, or question answering, while general-purpose alignment between Earth system data and language remains underexplored due to the limited availability of diverse language supervision grounded in meteorological conditions. To fill this gap, we introduce EarthAlign, a large-scale dataset with broad geographic coverage spanning 2000-2024 that combines 10 expert-curated natural event and disaster data sources with climatology-derived normal-weather samples. Each sample includes temporal and geospatial information and four grounded caption styles aligned with 63-variable ERA5 meteorological data. Building on EarthAlign, we introduce MeteoLIP, a dual-encoder framework for learning aligned meteorology-language representations. MeteoLIP incorporates MetTok, which uses a geolocation- and time-conditioned query to aggregate variable-specific patch embeddings into a compact sequence of meteorology tokens. To comprehensively assess Earth system multimodal representations, we introduce three downstream tasks: cross-modal retrieval, weather-condition classification, and physical variable estimation. Our experiments show that MeteoLIP improves upon the corresponding CLIP and SigLIP baselines across these tasks. Further analyses highlight the importance of meteorological input, temporal and geospatial conditioning, and multi-style supervision for meteorology-language alignment. Thus, EarthAlign and MeteoLIP provide a foundation for learning and evaluating language-aligned representations of Earth system data. Our code, dataset, and weights are publicly available at https://github.com/mbzuai-oryx/EarthAlign.

title: From Existing Methods to New Research Ideas: Two Perspectives on Recursive Self-Improvement
shortTitle: From Existing Methods to New Research Ideas: Two Perspectives on Recursive Self-Improvement
abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) offers a route to AI systems that participate in their own continued development. Recent methods allow language agents to retain changes to their parameters, memory, skills, and code for subsequent execution and improvement. We examine how these methods can inform new research ideas through two complementary perspectives. First, we introduce a unified taxonomy with nine design dimensions organized into four groups: update targets, update organization, update schedule and scope, feedback and selection. This taxonomy places existing methods in a shared design space, where examining individual dimensions and their interactions can inspire new research ideas. Second, we examine how existing RSI methods draw on traditional deep learning, for example through optimization, regularization, data augmentation, continual learning, and adversarial learning. We develop further ideas by examining more specific learning mechanisms and drawing on evolutionary computation. We also review how existing benchmarks assess self-improvement under online, offline, and offline-to-online settings. Together, these perspectives help researchers develop new RSI research ideas from existing designs and learning mechanisms. RSI papers and resources are available at https://prism-shadow.github.io/awesome-rsi/.

title: DuSRFlow: Dual-Lens Super-Resolution via Parallax-Aware Flow Estimation and Complementary Reference Warping
shortTitle: DuSRFlow: Dual-Lens Super-Resolution via Parallax-Aware Flow Estimation and Complementary Reference Warping
abstract: Dual-lens super-resolution (DuSR) aims to enhance a wide-angle low-resolution (LR) image by exploiting a telephoto reference (Ref) image. A central challenge in DuSR is reliable reference utilization under large parallax, occlusion, and cross-camera imaging discrepancies. Existing methods often employ off-the-shelf monocular optical flow models to provide geometric priors. However, their assumptions of photometric consistency and smooth motion are violated in dual-lens scenarios, leading to unreliable alignment and degraded reference-based reconstruction. To address these issues, we propose DuSRFlow, a dual-lens super-resolution framework that improves reference utilization from both correspondence learning and reference aggregation. First, we introduce DuFlowNet, a dedicated dual-lens flow estimator for robust cross-view alignment. To train DuFlowNet without ground-truth flow annotations, we develop a real--synthetic data fusion strategy that composites synthetic foreground objects onto real dual-lens image pairs, generating controllable large-parallax samples while preserving realistic cross-camera imaging characteristics. Second, we observe that reference reliability is highly spatially uneven in DuSR, where unreliable local reference responses may suppress the utilization of reliable cues. We therefore propose a Complementary Reference Warping strategy that coordinates patch-based warping and kernel-free-guided deformable warping according to local reference reliability, producing a more reliable reference representation before LR--Ref fusion. In addition, we construct DuSR-RealV2, a challenging real-world benchmark with complex depth variations, large parallax, and occlusion. Extensive experiments on multiple DuSR benchmarks demonstrate that DuSRFlow achieves state-of-the-art performance in reconstruction quality, perceptual quality, and cross-dataset generalization.

title: The Company a Question Keeps: Auditing Open Jev-Style Models for Retrieval
shortTitle: The Company a Question Keeps: Auditing Open Jev-Style Models for Retrieval
abstract: Jev's documented interface evaluates typed questions independently against shared evidence. We audit request independence in seven open Jev-style checkpoints on 276 constructed three-passage states from 92 TREC retrieval queries. Paired interventions separately change requested questions, displayed evidence, and candidate eligibility. Request expansion induces strict binary flips in 9.1%/8.0% of Nimble's judgments and changes 21.4%/18.9% of selection-or-abstention actions in TREC DL2019/2020 under a threshold of 0.5 fixed before inference. Correct-action rates change by 0.0/+8.2 percentage points, respectively, with 95% query-bootstrap intervals of [-6.0,6.0] and [3.8,12.6]. Field masking traces all 70 request-set flips to the schema fields serialized into each scoring prompt. In Von, fixing a shared separator's position eliminates two eligibility-induced preference flips in selected diagnostic states. Laya-typed's default CUDA path produces five passage swaps without strict binary flips, and both yearly action-change intervals include zero; in an FP32 rerun, its probability movement vanishes at the model's four-decimal reporting resolution.

title: Automatic assembly modeling through attention-based assembly feature mate prediction and assembly feature pattern recognition
shortTitle: Automatic assembly modeling through attention-based assembly feature mate prediction and assembly feature pattern recognition
abstract: Assembly modeling plays an important role in constructing product models, yet it is still mainly performed via interactive operations that are experience-dependent and labor-intensive. Data-driven strategies hold promise for automating this process; however, existing approaches either predict poses that cannot directly generate editable B-Rep assembly constraints or require prescribed part pairs or predefined assembly faces. To reduce the large candidate space of constraint prediction without predefined assembly faces, we propose a data-driven framework based on assembly feature mate prediction. The framework performs automatic assembly modeling from unassembled B-Rep parts, using assembly features to group the geometric entities of local mating interfaces and restrict candidate formation. Given the lack of suitable assembly feature annotations in existing datasets, we construct a large-scale dataset through an automatic annotation pipeline. Using the annotated dataset, we train an attention-based network to predict assembly feature mates, with Engineering Compatibility Fusion (ECF) incorporating explicit engineering compatibility into learned matching scores. To improve the accuracy of automatic assembly modeling, we use assembly feature patterns (AFPs) to guide the matching process. Finally, a post-processing search selects assembly feature mate and AFP mate candidates, whose associated constraints are generated and solved to complete assembly modeling. Experimental results show that the framework achieves assembly constraint accuracies of 74.79% on the six-assembly comparison set and 64.09% on the extended test set of 16 assemblies, which includes the comparison set. With ground-truth face labels supplied as additional input, the corresponding accuracies increase to 81.78% and 80.93%, respectively.

title: VbotNav-0: Asynchronous Cloud-Edge Dual-Policy Navigation across Indoor and Outdoor Environments
shortTitle: VbotNav-0: Asynchronous Cloud-Edge Dual-Policy Navigation across Indoor and Outdoor Environments
abstract: Continuous indoor-outdoor navigation connects destination-level reasoning with motion decisions that must respond to current observations. We present VbotNav-0, a cloud-edge dual-policy framework that links these processes through asynchronous policy-to-policy conditioning. The cloud policy produces subgoal guidance from visual history, navigation instructions, and route tokens; the edge policy combines available guidance with current RGB and LiDAR observations to generate local trajectories. This formulation allows the local perception-action loop to continue between cloud updates. A common route representation connects indoor paths and outdoor map routes, and the training recipe combines navigation demonstrations, corrective data, and grounded visual question answering (VQA). In the reported closed-loop evaluation of 258 episodes across 145 scenes, VbotNav-0 achieves 55.04% success rate and 55.03% success weighted by path length.

title: PVFH-Bench: Benchmarking Premise-Induced Visual Fixation Hallucinations in Vision-Language Models
shortTitle: PVFH-Bench: Benchmarking Premise-Induced Visual Fixation Hallucinations in Vision-Language Models
abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) have achieved remarkable progress across a wide range of multimodal tasks. However, object hallucination remains a persistent challenge, undermining model reliability in applications such as visual question answering, embodied agents, and human-AI decision support systems. In this paper, inspired by cognitive science studies on perceptual bias, we investigate a new failure mode termed Premise-Induced Visual Fixation Hallucination (PVFH). Specifically, PVFH refers to a premise-induced reasoning error in which models become anchored to visually confusable evidence, accept a false textual premise, and subsequently generate responses about an absent yet visually plausible object. To systematically study this phenomenon, we introduce PVFH-Bench, a benchmark that automatically constructs visually confusable but absent targets and pairs the core hallucination setting with diagnostic subsets to trace how models move from object recognition to Premise-Induced Visual Fixation Hallucination. Experimental results on 10 state-of-the-art LVLMs demonstrate that all evaluated models are highly vulnerable to Premise-Induced Visual Fixation Hallucination. Moreover, we find that explicit chain-of-thought reasoning can further exacerbate this failure mode by encouraging models to overinterpret weak visual cues as supporting evidence for hallucinated objects.

title: PEARL: Process-Experience Aware Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Turn Agents
shortTitle: PEARL: Process-Experience Aware Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Turn Agents
abstract: Terminal rewards make multi-turn agents trainable without step-level annotations, but group-relative advantages provide little guidance about which intermediate decisions to adjust. Failed trajectories also contain reasonable actions, while unfavorable decision patterns can recur as training proceeds. We introduce PEARL (Process-Experience Aware Reinforcement Learning), which improves local credit assignment without an additional critic. Given two continuations from the same history with different outcomes, PEARL locates their first divergence and builds a feature representation of each branch's local decision. It clusters these decision features in recent failure and success memories to identify recurring local patterns. Using this pattern memory, PEARL selectively strengthens negative advantages at lower-reward decisions, while leaving positive advantages and the base policy optimizer unchanged. On AppWorld, PEARL improves over ARPO on Normal and Challenge tasks at both 4B and 8B scales. On ALFWorld, it achieves 97.9% mean success at 4B, 2.7 points above the strongest baseline, while remaining competitive at 8B. Ablations of shaping location, success-bank filtering, and memory window support the value of selective, recurring-pattern-based updates.

title: Shaping Latent Mixture-of-Experts: From Expert Geometry to Layerwise Capacity Allocation
shortTitle: Shaping Latent Mixture-of-Experts: From Expert Geometry to Layerwise Capacity Allocation
abstract: Fine-grained mixture-of-experts (MoE) models commonly increase expert count by narrowing each expert, treating expert shape as a by-product of routing granularity. LatentMoE moves expert computation into a lower-dimensional space, exposing the input dimension and intermediate width of each expert as explicit design choices. We show that an expert's local Jacobian rank is jointly bounded by these two dimensions, and that balancing them maximizes the rank ceiling at fixed per-expert parameters. Controlled shape sweeps across model scales and routing granularities consistently favor near-square experts. We further use layerwise intrinsic dimension (ID) to guide capacity allocation across depth, co-varying the number and shape of experts while keeping per-layer parameter count, activated FLOPs, and communication volume constant. Compared with layer-homogeneous baselines, our ID-guided allocation achieves lower validation loss and stronger downstream performance. These results establish expert shape and layerwise allocation as practical design axes for MoEs.

title: Can Synthetic UAV Benchmarks Be Trusted? Real-Synthetic Validation for UAV Model Selection
shortTitle: Can Synthetic UAV Benchmarks Be Trusted? Real-Synthetic Validation for UAV Model Selection
abstract: Synthetic UAV imagery can expand pre-deployment test evidence when task-specific Real data are scarce, but visual plausibility or semantic label alignment alone does not establish validity for model selection. In contrast, a closed-set stress test on a separately materialized business corpus, using four VisDrone-compatible detectors over eight empirically supported classes, changes the point-estimate top-ranked detector and reverses three of six pairwise point-estimate preference directions. A complementary audit of five UAV business scenarios further reveals substantial Real-Synthetic mismatch in class composition, object density, and target scale, including systematic under-representation of small targets. These results show that Synthetic UAV benchmark trust is conditional: semantic coverage is insufficient, and validity must be established empirically for the task, operating regime, and model panel of interest.

title: TAG: Calibrating SAM3 for Universal Image Segmentation without Dense Supervision
shortTitle: TAG: Calibrating SAM3 for Universal Image Segmentation without Dense Supervision
abstract: The recent Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM3) extends powerful promptable segmentation from spatial cues to concepts, raising the prospect of a single foundation model for universal image segmentation. However, this promise often fails to translate into reliable performance on downstream segmentation tasks. In this work, we empirically identify concept recognition, rather than mask quality, as the primary bottleneck: SAM3 accurately delineates the objects it recognizes yet struggles to robustly determine which concepts are present. Driven by this, we present \textit{\underline{T}ext \underline{A}nchor re-\underline{G}rounding (\TAG{})}, a simple yet effective framework that rectifies the concept recognition of SAM3 on the target domain without dense annotations. Specifically, \TAG{} introduces an \textit{Anchor Residual Pathway} comprising image-conditioned, low-rank adapters to re-ground text anchors in the target distribution and modulate subsequent text-conditioned interactions. Guided solely by image-level category labels, \TAG{} jointly optimizes binary cross-entropy with \textit{Soft Boundary Ranking} objectives to calibrate presence confidence and distinguish present concepts from confusable negatives. Building upon this, we devise \textit{Confidence-Weighted Distillation} to couple rich semantic context of a multimodal large language model with fine-grained spatial priors of SAM3, thereby achieving effective calibration in the absence of manual annotations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that \TAG{} unlocks SAM3's segmentation potential with only 3.1M trainable parameters, achieving impressive performance across diverse scenarios, and notably, even surpassing leading mask-supervised methods on several metrics. \href{https://github.com/MiSsU-HH/TAG_SAM3}{Our code will be publicly available at GitHub \faGithub}.

title: Prospective Forcing: Learning to Look Ahead for Autoregressive Long Video Diffusion
shortTitle: Prospective Forcing: Learning to Look Ahead for Autoregressive Long Video Diffusion
abstract: Autoregressive video generators synthesize long videos through chunk-wise rollouts, yet they are typically trained to predict only the immediate future. This limited prediction horizon makes it challenging to maintain video quality over extended rollouts. To address this problem, we introduce Prospective Forcing, a multi-head prediction framework that injects long-range predictive signals into autoregressive video representations. Built on a rolling-window generator, Prospective Forcing attaches lightweight, offset-specific heads that share the same conditioning information and independently predict chunks at different future temporal offsets. By extending supervision beyond the next chunk, these heads encourage the shared history representation to retain information useful for longer-horizon prediction, supporting temporally consistent generation. At inference time, we accelerate sampling by using accepted future-chunk predictions to skip full-window backbone executions. We equip the head with learnable embeddings to generate multiple candidates for the next chunk, and a learned verifier either selects a candidate or rejects all and falls back to standard autoregressive generation.

title: Global Optimality of Pose Graph Optimization
shortTitle: Global Optimality of Pose Graph Optimization
abstract: Pose Graph Optimization (PGO) is a classical and widely applied problem in state estimation for robotics, playing a fundamental role in localization, mapping, and navigation. Yet, it is nonconvex in nature and may have many local minimizers, thus difficult to analyze. In this paper, we investigate the optimization landscape and establish a sufficient condition of global optimality for PGO. The ultimate goal of this paper is to theoretically confirm that the optimization landscape is benign and attractive around the global minimizer, if noise is smaller than an explicit and a priori bound. To reveal such an insight, this paper develops three main technical results. First, we identify a proper basin of attraction (BOA) containing global minimizer, and characterize its geometric property by showing that its radius is controlled by noise in an explicit way. Then, by exploring the first order optimality conditions of PGO, we prove that a local minimizer is globally optimal if a noise-controlled criterion is satisfied. Finally, by combining above two results, we prove that one and only one local minimizer exists in the BOA and this minimizer is globally optimal, when the noise is smaller than an explicit bound that can be verified a priori. Numerical simulations validate the proposed theory under various random cases, showing that the obtained conditions provide an effective criterion for certifying the global optimality of PGO.

title: TGuide: Faster Autoregressive Video Diffusion via Historical Trajectory Guidance
shortTitle: TGuide: Faster Autoregressive Video Diffusion via Historical Trajectory Guidance
abstract: Can autoregressive video diffusion be accelerated further when only four denoising steps remain? Existing feature caching approaches struggle in this regime, as large feature changes between denoising timesteps undermine both direct reuse and lightweight predictors. We observe that features across video chunks remain strongly correlated at matching denoising timesteps, offering a complementary source of guidance. Building on this insight, we introduce TGuide, a framework that accelerates autoregressive video diffusion through a lightweight Anchor-Transport-Correct (ATC) predictor guided by historical sampling trajectories. Our ATC combines two complementary references: the current chunk's preceding-step features preserve its spatial structure, while the previous chunk's same-timestep features provide information at the target denoising stage. By integrating these references through spatial retrieval and adaptive correction, ATC improves velocity prediction accuracy despite the large gaps between denoising steps. To mitigate error accumulation across both denoising steps and video chunks, we train the predictor on its own autoregressive rollouts, allowing it to adapt to states shaped by its own earlier predictions. An optional confidence-aware scheduler further adjusts the quality-efficiency trade-off. Experiments on Self Forcing, Causal Forcing, and HY-WorldPlay show that TGuide preserves generation quality while achieving denoising speedups of up to $1.89\times$ over the original 4-step generators. On Self Forcing, TGuide generalizes from 81-frame training videos to 333-frame generation, approximately four times the training length, while exceeding the original model's VBench score.

title: TETRIS-4DGS: Efficient Post-Training Compression of 4D Gaussian Splatting
shortTitle: TETRIS-4DGS: Efficient Post-Training Compression of 4D Gaussian Splatting
abstract: 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS) has emerged as a powerful dynamic scene representation, supporting real-time high quality rendering but suffers from prohibitive storage overhead. Existing methods typically attempt to solve this by treating compression as a per-scene optimization problem, limiting generalizability and applicability where low-latency compression is required. In this work, we leverage existing image and video codecs and propose a generalized post-training compression framework for 4DGS to address these issues. Specifically, we apply importance-based adaptive quantization to Gaussians according to their importance levels, effectively refining bitrate allocation while remaining fully compatible with existing codecs. To further improve compression efficiency, we utilize the statistical properties of 4DGS and propose motion- and importance-aware packing to reorganize attributes into codec-friendly 2D maps. Our approach can achieve over 40x compression rate in seconds while maintaining high quality, facilitating the practical deployment of 4DGS.

title: SPARE: Shared Perception and Adaptive Retrieval of Evidence for Streaming Video Understanding
shortTitle: SPARE: Shared Perception and Adaptive Retrieval of Evidence for Streaming Video Understanding
abstract: Streaming video understanding requires answering questions from the observed video, with evidence drawn from recent observations or earlier events. Historical context can improve recall but may interfere with judgments based on recent frames. Its usefulness depends on both when it is introduced and which clips are selected, while relevance alone does not guarantee sufficient evidence for an answer. We propose SPARE, a framework that combines adaptive historical retrieval with visual encoder sharing. A lightweight gate predicts whether recent observations provide sufficient evidence to answer the question. When additional evidence is predicted to be necessary, a multimodal embedding model retrieves relevant historical clips to supplement the current context. LoRA instruction tuning trains the understanding model to use recent observations and retrieved history jointly and abstain when the evidence remains insufficient. To reduce redundant visual parameters, the understanding and retrieval branches share a visual encoder while retaining separate language backbones. Four linear adapters align the shared features with the retrieval model through distillation at the visual token and final retrieval embedding levels. With visual-only inputs, SPARE achieves 77.78% on the evaluated Real-time and Backward task groups of OVO-Bench and 73.31% on StreamingBench. Compared with Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct evaluated at 2 fps, SPARE improves accuracy by 20.68 percentage points on OVO-Bench and 14.15 percentage points on StreamingBench.

title: Competition Domains Matter: Selective Head Globalization for Training-Free Sparse Attention in Video Diffusion Transformers
shortTitle: Competition Domains Matter: Selective Head Globalization for Training-Free Sparse Attention in Video Diffusion Transformers
abstract: Training-free sparse attention is a practical route to efficient video diffusion transformer inference, yet existing methods typically fix the competition domain at each query row for every attention head. We introduce EG-Sparse, a training-free framework that routes low-entropy heads to a grouped cross-head pool while retaining per-row local selection for high-entropy heads, using only scores already materialized by the sparse pipeline. A controlled diagnostic fixes the ranking score and varies only the competition rule: grouped cross-head selection reduces low-entropy-head reconstruction error by 9.8%, whereas forcing high-entropy heads into an all-head global pool increases it by 7.9%. Across four configurations, EG-Sparse achieves higher video quality while reducing attention density and GPU denoising latency compared with strong training-free sparse-attention baselines. Mechanism ablations further show that selective domain adaptation outperforms uniform, random, and fixed domain-assignment policies. These results support competition-domain adaptation as a distinct design axis within centroid-guided training-free sparse attention.

title: CAST-ASD: Causal Attention over Speakers and Time for Online Active Speaker Detection
shortTitle: CAST-ASD: Causal Attention over Speakers and Time for Online Active Speaker Detection
abstract: We present CAST-ASD (Causal Attention over Speakers and Time), a causal joint model for active speaker detection (ASD). Recent ASD models improve performance by jointly processing all faces in a scene, but operate offline, with the full clip available before any frame is labelled. Low-latency causal detectors instead process each face independently. CAST-ASD combines joint face reasoning with fully causal inference. It applies scene-level attention across faces within the current frame and causal temporal attention over each face's history, enabling information sharing across speakers with zero lookahead. Its parameter count does not grow with the number of faces. On MSDWild, where most negative face-frames contain a visible competing speaker, CAST-ASD reduces competing-speaker false alarms by 32% relative to the causal per-face detector it extends, with larger gains as scene occupancy increases. It outperforms all causal baselines on both validation splits while using only one-tenth the inter-speaker parameters of a three-block fixed-roster convolution. title: HumanPhys: A Human-Centric Physical-World Perception Benchmark for Real-World Visual Reasoning
shortTitle: HumanPhys: A Human-Centric Physical-World Perception Benchmark for Real-World Visual Reasoning
abstract: We introduce HumanPhys, a human-centric benchmark for real-world physical perception, and a training corpus emitted by the same pipeline. Each question targets a physically grounded quantity related to people, including depth, inter-person distance, gaze angle, displacement, velocity, heading-step trajectory, blink count, and contact-deformation strength. The rendered probes additionally test illumination inference from body and face cues and camera ego-motion, both with and without a person in the frame. All labels are derived programmatically from sensor calibration, source metadata, or renderer state, rather than written by annotators or produced by estimators on the benchmark frames. HumanPhys systematically probes six dimensions of human-centric physical perception: spatial state, kinematics, blink events, deformation, illumination, and camera pose. To the best of our knowledge, no existing MLLM benchmark-and-training corpus jointly supervises this set of human-centered physical quantities under direct metadata- or renderer-derived labels. The six dimensions appear only partially dissociable across the tested MLLMs. We benchmark a range of open- and closed-source MLLMs on HumanPhys and find that all six capability dimensions remain challenging for current models. We hope HumanPhys will support future research on multimodal systems that perceive and reason about people in the physical world.

title: A Hybrid Kinematic GCN and Elastic Transformer for Efficient Indian Sign Language Recognition
shortTitle: A Hybrid Kinematic GCN and Elastic Transformer for Efficient Indian Sign Language Recognition
abstract: Sign Language Recognition (SLR) presents complex challenges due to variable signing speeds and spatial intricacies. Specifically, Indian Sign Language (ISL) requires precise modeling of its inherently bimanual nature and is bottlenecked by the scarcity of large-vocabulary benchmarks and the inability of standard models to handle irregular signing velocities. To address this, a structurally-aware hybrid framework for efficient, gloss ISL recognition is proposed. To minimize computational redundancy, an entropy-driven SVD sampler that dynamically extracts informative keyframes is used. Because this subsampling creates irregular physical time gaps, the proposed architecture employs a Continuous Dual Positional Encoding paired with a distance-aware Elastic Transformer to preserve natural signing rhythm. Spatially, a Kinematically-Conditioned Adaptive GCN explicitly models bimanual geometry using unified bone-joint features. To validate our framework, a 120-class, 9,453-video native ISL dataset is created. Augmented by Physical Node Dropout and ArcFace optimization to mitigate subject-specific memorization, our framework achieves a competitive 89.8% accuracy, establishing a strong baseline for complex sign language modeling.

title: Successful but Unsafe: An Analytical Benchmark for Revealing Collisions in Vision-and-Language Navigation
shortTitle: Successful but Unsafe: An Analytical Benchmark for Revealing Collisions in Vision-and-Language Navigation
abstract: Vision-and-language navigation (VLN) agents are typically evaluated by whether they reach a target and how efficiently they follow an instructed route, yet these metrics provide little information about collision behavior. Moreover, continuous VLN evaluation commonly uses a sliding regime, where an agent can slide along obstacles after a collision, potentially masking the effect of unsafe actions on navigation performance. We introduce VLN-Safe, a benchmark for analyzing collision safety under two complementary evaluation regimes: sliding, reflecting common VLN evaluation practice, and blocking, where collision-inducing actions prevent forward motion and more directly expose their consequences. Across six published agents on R2R-CE, 38.5-56.8% of successful episodes contain contact under sliding, while switching to blocking decreases success rate by 11.7-36.1 percentage points. We further analyze signals for anticipating imminent collisions and find that depth geometry and recent movement history are more informative than policy-derived signals, while safe alternatives near the policy's preferred action are rarely available. Motivated by these findings, we introduce a training-free collision guard that vetoes risky forward actions, executes an escape maneuver, and returns control to the original policy. Under blocking, the guard reduces collision steps by 62-98% and improves success rate by 6.9-29.3 percentage points across five recurrent, topological, and vision-language-action agents. Under sliding, it leaves success rate unchanged while raising the share of collision-free successes by 4.1-12.4 points. These results reveal a substantial gap between task success and collision-safe navigation and show that lightweight collision-aware intervention can improve both safety and navigation performance.

title: Triage-PiEvo: Evidence Admission for Principle-Evolving Scientific Agents
shortTitle: Triage-PiEvo: Evidence Admission for Principle-Evolving Scientific Agents
abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based AI Scientists advance scientific discovery, yet they suffer from inefficiencies due to noisy observations. Existing principle-evolving agents act on every anomaly, leaving its source unresolved: a new mechanism or an evaluation artifact, so invalid revisions bias evolution. To address this, we formulate revision as evidence admission: anomalies steer search immediately, but only independently verified evidence may rewrite persistent principles, and contradicted principles are retracted. We realize this in TRIAGE-PIEVO , which pairs an anomaly-responsive search portfolio with a staged verification gate that alone controls what enters principle state. Across four scientific tasks with three backbones, TRIAGE-PIEVO (1) attains the highest average solution quality with +7.5%~11.8% over the strongest baseline per backbone, matching the strongest baseline's full-budget quality with one-third of the evaluation budget on Qwen3-235B; and additional stress tests and cross-harness deployment demonstrate that (2) in constructed stress tests, it admits none of the corrupted, hidden-source, or exploit evidence that ungated variants admit, while missing no planted mechanism, and (3) plugged unchanged into three external research harnesses, it cuts false evidence admissions by over 60% and raises verified scores by 31%~43%.

title: Demiurge: Forging Navigable 4D Worlds via Autoregressive Video Rerendering
shortTitle: Demiurge: Forging Navigable 4D Worlds via Autoregressive Video Rerendering
abstract: Recent advances in video diffusion enable novel-view video synthesis from a single input video, supporting world modeling, embodied intelligence, and robotic simulation. However, existing methods process camera trajectories independently, lacking the cross-trajectory consistency needed for coherent, navigable 4D worlds. We introduce Demiurge, an autoregressive video rerendering pipeline built on a dynamic 4D point-cloud memory cache. It promotes cross-trajectory consistency through four components: (1) an appearance video diffusion model that synthesizes photorealistic novel-view videos conditioned on the 4D memory; (2) a memory-consistent video depth completion model that aligns known-region depths with cached geometry and completes missing regions, mitigating scale ambiguity and discontinuities during memory updates; (3) memory-aware dual-stream warping that provides high-fidelity visual guidance and occlusion cues for novel-view synthesis; and (4) geometry-aware video refinement that enhances perceptual quality. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art performance and three key capabilities: coherent spatiotemporal lattice construction over dense multi-view trajectories; large-parallax video rerendering under challenging camera motions, including 180-degree rotations with no input-view overlap; and geometry-faithful outputs that can be directly optimized into high-quality 3D Gaussian Splatting representations with minimal artifacts. Project page: https://hanxinzhu-lab.github.io/demiurge_project_page/.

title: One-Way Coupling via Patchwise Adaptive Normalization in Transformer Surrogates
shortTitle: One-Way Coupling via Patchwise Adaptive Normalization in Transformer Surrogates
abstract: Many physical systems exhibit one-way coupling: exogenous fields such as medium density or obstacle geometry influence the dynamics without being affected by them. We investigate how explicitly representing these fields can improve the accuracy and computational efficiency of transformer-based PDE surrogates. Building on spatially adaptive normalization, we introduce Patchwise Adaptive Normalization (PAdaNorm), which partitions exogenous fields into patches aligned with the state tokenization. We evaluate PAdaNorm on datasets from three different domains, using a Walrus-inspired transformer architecture. Across the three PDE families, PAdaNorm is on par with or up to 16% better than parameter-matched baselines in mean long-horizon variance-scaled RMSE on 60-step autoregressive rollouts. We also find that PAdaNorm better maintains hard physical constraints over long rollouts, such as preventing flow into impenetrable solid regions in porous media. When the conditioning is static, PAdaNorm caches the conditioning embeddings once and reuses them across the entire rollout, reducing inference FLOPs per step by up to 36% compared with parameter-matched baselines. An ablation over eight conditioning variants shows that modulating a single attention axis (temporal or spatial) suffices and that a lightweight shared MLP across blocks remains competitive with per-block projections.

title: Accelerating Cross-Model LLM Inference via Attention Map Reuse
shortTitle: Accelerating Cross-Model LLM Inference via Attention Map Reuse
abstract: LLM-augmented data workflows often involve multiple heterogeneous models operating over substantial shared context, such as schemas, tool specifications, interaction history, and intermediate results. Although prefix caching can reduce prefilling overhead, existing approaches are largely limited to reuse within the same model because KV states are tightly coupled to model-specific architectures. We present MapFlow, a system for efficient heterogeneous LLM serving via cross-model attention map reuse. Instead of reusing KV states, MapFlow reuses attention maps, which capture token dependency patterns and are more transferable across models. To enable efficient and accurate reuse, we combine partial recomputation with lightweight linear translation across layers and heads. To make attention reuse practical for long contexts, we further introduce block-level sparse compression and a fused retrieval kernel. Experiments show that MapFlow reduces prefilling latency and improves end-to-end serving efficiency while preserving generation quality across heterogeneous model pairs and multi-turn routing workloads. These results suggest that attention maps provide an effective reusable state for heterogeneous LLM serving, especially in prefix-heavy data workflows. Our code is available: https://github.com/PKU-DAIR/MapFlow.

title: DexCast: Learning Real-World Dexterous Control from Human Videos
shortTitle: DexCast: Learning Real-World Dexterous Control from Human Videos
abstract: Recent advances in 3D hand-object interaction (HOI) perception have opened new opportunities for learning dexterous robotic skills from human videos. However, existing dexterous imitation learning methods often rely on costly and manually teleoperated robot demonstrations, requiring substantial human effort. Therefore, we build DEXCAST, a framework that learns dexterous robotic hand control directly from monocular RGB-D videos by leveraging joint HOI reconstructions, without requiring any teleoperation. Furthermore, how to model high-dimensional robotic hand motion and extract temporal context to inform future action generation remains a key challenge. To this end, we propose a DexHand Motion Perception Module (DMPM) to capture inter-joint coordination and temporal dependencies in compact latent representations that condition our diffusion policy. Extensive real-world experiments demonstrate that DEXCAST achieves exceptional performance across diverse dexterous manipulation tasks.

title: AcrossVAM2.0: Conflict-Aware Point Supervision for Parameter-Efficient Video Diffusion Adaptation
shortTitle: AcrossVAM2.0: Conflict-Aware Point Supervision for Parameter-Efficient Video Diffusion Adaptation
abstract: Explicit point correspondence is attractive for adapting video generators: it describes how visible surfaces move, but can overwrite the appearance prior learned by a large pretrained model. We study this tension in a 5.01B-parameter text-to-video diffusion transformer. ACROSSVAM2.0 combines a confidence-weighted track-and-visibility head, zero-initialized residual feedback, and asymmetric PCGrad that removes only the auxiliary component opposing the primary flow-matching gradient on shared LoRA parameters. The design preserves the generator exactly at initialization and protects its primary update during adaptation. In a four-way ablation trained for 1,000 steps with three independent seeds, the full method lowers KLT forward-backward cycle error in all three seeds relative to a matched flow-only continuation (mean seed-level difference -0.00711, SD 0.00505), while robust sharpness remains positive in all three. An expanded 24-prompt evaluation (216 videos) yields 9.7% lower aggregate CoTracker3 cycle error than the matched control and near-matched performance on six VBench dimensions; however, the seed-level tracking effect is heterogeneous and I3D-FVD regresses from 0.1824 to 0.2022. These results support a bounded claim: conflict-aware adaptation improves correspondence consistency without broad perceptual degradation, but does not uniformly improve video quality. We release equations, pseudocode, matched outputs, source tables, and artifact provenance.

title: VoTSpeech: Decoupling Voice Design from Speech Generation in Instruction-Following TTS
shortTitle: VoTSpeech: Decoupling Voice Design from Speech Generation in Instruction-Following TTS
abstract: Instruction-following text-to-speech (TTS) typically leaves voice design implicit, as conventional speaker embeddings encode reference audio rather than text-driven targets. We propose VoTSpeech, which decouples voice design from speech generation via an explicit intermediate voice latent. Built on a shared language model backbone, VoTSpeech first predicts a continuous voice latent from text instructions using a flow-based module. This latent serves as a shared condition for both the language model and the Acoustic DiT, guiding autoregressive sequence modeling and acoustic latent generation, respectively, before an audio VAE decoder converts the acoustic latents into waveforms. To capture speaker identity and complementary acoustic nuances, the voice latent is jointly supervised by speaker embeddings and temporally pooled audio VAE features. With task-specific adaptation, VoTSpeech performs strongly on InstructTTSEval-ZH, demonstrating competitive capabilities against strong open-source models while maintaining high naturalness. These results confirm that explicit voice latent design and its conditioning interface effectively empower text-driven voice design for controllable speech synthesis. Code, model, and audio samples are available at https://github.com/ywbn/VoTSpeech .

title: Understanding Hidden Spatial Preferences in Bayesian Optimization
shortTitle: Understanding Hidden Spatial Preferences in Bayesian Optimization
abstract: Bayesian optimization uses posterior uncertainty to decide where to explore, but this uncertainty is not spatially neutral. On bounded domains, Gaussian-process posterior variance is typically larger near faces, edges, and corners, giving variance-based acquisition functions a systematic boundary bias. This spatial preference is usually inherited from the surrogate rather than chosen as part of the exploration strategy. We separate these roles by keeping the predictive model fixed and modifying the spatial preference of the exploration term. We control the preference with spatial weight fields and amortize their construction with neural surrogates. Controlled experiments show that the Gaussian process' default boundary bias changes which parts of the domain are explored and which optima are reached. We compare three alternative exploration principles and find, across standard benchmark functions and stochastic robot-pushing tasks, that they can often lower regret, particularly early in the optimization. The spatial structure of posterior uncertainty is therefore not a neutral default: it shapes the exploration strategy and can materially affect optimization performance.

title: AlignAudio: A Unified Dual-Alignment Framework for Noise-Robust Speech-Conditioned Generation
shortTitle: AlignAudio: A Unified Dual-Alignment Framework for Noise-Robust Speech-Conditioned Generation
abstract: Speech-conditioned generation maps speech signals to target audio outputs. Prior end-to-end speech-conditioned generative models achieve high fidelity in clean acoustic conditions, but their performance degrades substantially under environmental noise. While prior noise-robust approaches have achieved significant success in feature-level purification, maintaining consistent generation under clean and noisy conditioning remains a key challenge. To address this, we propose AlignAudio, a noise-robust generative framework based on dual alignment: (i) aligning the representations of clean and noisy speech to preserve semantic cues, and (ii) enforcing generation-level consistency within a flow matching paradigm to improve conditioning fidelity. Experiments on speech-to-audio (STA) and voice conversion (VC) tasks demonstrate that AlignAudio maintains performance comparable to baselines on clean speech while significantly outperforming them across various noisy conditions. Furthermore, the proposed dual-alignment strategy is applicable to both single- and multi-stream speech conditioning and can be integrated into different flow matching-based generation frameworks and post-training settings. title: PURE: Refining Feed-forward 3D Reconstruction with Unlabeled Post-training
shortTitle: PURE: Refining Feed-forward 3D Reconstruction with Unlabeled Post-training
abstract: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction models have achieved remarkable progress through large-scale training and strong learned priors. However, they remain fragile when applied to dynamic in-the-wild videos, where non-rigid motion, occlusions, and illumination changes are prevalent. A key limitation lies in their reliance on expensive depth and camera pose annotations, which hinders scaling to diverse real-world dynamic data and restricts generalization. To address this issue, we propose \textbf{PURE}, an unlabeled post-training refinement framework that improves depth and camera estimation without requiring ground-truth supervision. Instead of relying on annotations, PURE elegantly distills robust structural knowledge from state-of-the-art 2D priors into 4D feed-forward architectures. PURE leverages relative depth constraints, affine-invariant geometry distillation, and pose refinement based on feature correspondences to stabilize geometric predictions under challenging dynamic conditions. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world dynamic benchmarks demonstrate that PURE delivers consistent improvements across multiple state-of-the-art architectures. Furthermore, our data-efficient paradigm effectively mitigates domain shifts, successfully unlocking the architectural limits of these base models in challenging, in-the-wild dynamic scenes.

title: Joint Discrete and SE(3) Diffusion for Protein Interface Design
shortTitle: Joint Discrete and SE(3) Diffusion for Protein Interface Design
abstract: The design of high-affinity, target-specific protein binders is central to the development of modern therapeutics. However, existing protein-generation methods remain limited in this setting, as many generated designs fail to simultaneously achieve geometric and physicochemical complementarity at binding interfaces. To address this challenge, we introduce PIDiff, a physicochemically enhanced multimodal diffusion framework for protein-protein complex design. PIDiff jointly designs target-conditioned protein sequences and structures by coupling diffusion in discrete sequence space with diffusion on the continuous (SE(3)) structural manifold. At its core, PIDiff employs PIFormer, a novel architecture that interleaves geometry-aware invariant point attention with global sequence self-attention. We further curate PIBench, a protein-protein complex dataset with diverse target scaffolds derived from the Protein Data Bank (PDB). We first pretrain PIDiff on PIBench and subsequently fine-tune it for two therapeutically relevant applications: minibinder design and antibody design. PPFrame consistently outperforms baseline methods across sequence design success rate, structure binding energy, and sequence-structure co-designability on all tasks.

title: DSABench: Benchmarking Source Discovery, Coordination, and Execution for Multi-Database Agents
shortTitle: DSABench: Benchmarking Source Discovery, Coordination, and Execution for Multi-Database Agents
abstract: Most text-to-SQL benchmarks provide the target database. In a large data catalog, however, choosing the sources is part of the problem: an agent must find every database needed for a request, determine how their results fit together, and execute the resulting workflow. We present DSABench to evaluate these capabilities jointly. Its 815 human-reviewed tasks draw on Spider, BIRD, and LiveSQLBench; 618 require several databases to contribute, and 105 allow more than one interpretation of the required sources. Executable contracts define source participation, cross-source dependencies, and source-local execution, while RouteEnv lets agents inspect public catalog evidence without revealing the gold annotations. In our routing-only study across seven model backends, the highest RA-Set score is 60.55%, compared with a highest RA-Graph score of 34.66% when coordination requirements are included. The gap becomes more pronounced when execution is required. Across four backends, median non-privileged Route+Exec-Graph success ranges from 6.69% to 7.98% without clarification and from 11.44% to 13.25% with one clarification; the best observed clarified configuration reaches 16.99%. On ambiguous tasks, clarification improves exact branch-source recovery by 39.8-43.2 percentage points. These findings illustrate why retrieving plausible databases or producing correct local SQL is not enough: an agent must carry the right information through the entire multi-database workflow.

title: Towards Merging-conditional Backdoor Unalignment against Large Language Models
shortTitle: Towards Merging-conditional Backdoor Unalignment against Large Language Models
abstract: Model merging has become widely adopted for enhancing the task-specific performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) without additional training. While the specialized model from third-party platforms may undergo safety audits (e.g., backdoor detection), we reveal a novel and critical threat: One-sided Merging-Conditional Backdoor (OMCB). OMCB remains dormant and undetectable within one standalone model but activates upon merging, triggering safety unalignment. We first theoretically analyze the existence and geometric location of OMCB, revealing that the parameter shift crossing safety decision boundaries is the main cause of backdoor activation. Building upon this insight, we propose SMOKE, a meta-learning-based attack framework. SMOKE implants OMCB via a bi-level optimization strategy: the inner loop synthesizes surrogate meta-vectors through random low-rank initialization and finite-step maximization, while the outer loop optimizes the target model by simulating the merging process. Furthermore, preliminary analysis shows that the injected OMCB has bounded generalization loss under unknown merging configurations. Extensive experiments across diverse model architectures and merging techniques validate the effectiveness of SMOKE and its resistance to existing backdoor detections, highlighting a significant yet previously overlooked vulnerability in the model merging paradigm.

title: BGC-Nav: Cross-Altitude Multi-UAV Collaborative Navigation via Belief-Guided Coupling
shortTitle: BGC-Nav: Cross-Altitude Multi-UAV Collaborative Navigation via Belief-Guided Coupling
abstract: Despite recent advances in Aerial Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN), single Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) search-and-rescue in outdoor scenarios remains challenging due to partial observability, making cross-altitude collaboration a promising direction. However, existing collaborative navigation methods rely on precise target localization and rigid goal-dispatching paradigms, ignoring high-altitude observation uncertainty and suppressing low-altitude exploration autonomy. To address these issues, we introduce BGC-Nav, a training-free cross-altitude collaboration framework that enables robust navigation via Belief-Guided Coupling (BGC). Specifically, the high-altitude UAV maintains a Global Belief Memory encoding task-conditioned priors, which the low-altitude agent incorporates into decision-making via Local Exhaustion Memory (LEM), Local Attraction Augmentation (LAA), and Directional Belief Prior (DBP) as an advisory bias rather than a rigid command. Extensive experiments on ESARBench show that BGC-Nav consistently outperforms state-of-the-art single-agent and collaborative methods. Code is available at https://github.com/uestchjw/BGC-Nav.

title: Linear-Time Non-Local Codec Placement for Machine Learning Model Compression
shortTitle: Linear-Time Non-Local Codec Placement for Machine Learning Model Compression
abstract: On-device inference imposes constraints on model storage and operand traffic and thus benefits from compressed operand representations, which mandate the use of encoding and decoding operators. However, na\"ıve placement of codec operators can cancel the operand traffic gains sought from compression. In this work, I present an algorithm to place codec operators into a source computational graph to make it compatible with target hardware. The edges of the graph are colored so that each induced subgraph is weakly connected and has a maximal node that both postdominates all subgraph inputs and dominates all subgraph outputs; this unique node - dubbed the $\textit{absolute dominator}$ - is the natural location to observe the traffic flowing through the subgraph and learn parametric codec operators. The algorithm's time complexity is linear in the source graph's size. With respect to na\"ıve local codec placement, the algorithm reduces modeled operand traffic by $24\%$-$44\%$ across four models, including $24\%$ on SigLIP and $34\%$ on SmolLM2.

title: PRISM: Precision Forcing for Generalist Vision-Language-Action Policies
shortTitle: PRISM: Precision Forcing for Generalist Vision-Language-Action Policies
abstract: Coupling a pretrained vision-language model (VLM) with a diffusion or flow-matching action expert has become the mainstream vision-language-action (VLA) paradigm for embodied policies, yet they remain unreliable once a task demands precise manipulation, e.g., submillimeter cable insertion. We attribute this weakness to a training objective that averages flow-matching errors across contexts and flow times, allocating little supervision to the few decisive moments determining task success. Along the generative path, inference integrates a locally supervised velocity field, so equally penalized errors at different flow times can affect the executed action unequally. Consequently, precision-task performance deteriorates as physical tolerance tightens by orders of magnitude. We call this supervision imbalance across contexts and flow times Flow-Time Starvation. The remedy is to jointly align supervision allocation and representation learning with context-dependent precision demand, enabling the policy to recognize when greater precision is needed. We instantiate this precision-forcing strategy as Precision-aware Reweighting and Internalization for Skilled Manipulation (PRISM), which scores precision demand offline, strengthens flow supervision where errors are consequential and action signals are visible, and internalizes that demand in the VLM condition representation. Simulation and real-robot experiments show that PRISM preserves or improves general-task performance while raising mean end-to-end success from 38.3% to 86.7% across drive connector insertion, bimanual connector mating, and screw tightening, substantially extending the precision boundary of existing embodied policies without new sensors or observation modalities.

title: Lingdan-V2: Large language models for clinically grounded reasoning in traditional Chinese medicine
shortTitle: Lingdan-V2: Large language models for clinically grounded reasoning in traditional Chinese medicine
abstract: Large language models have advanced medical reasoning, but clinically grounded reasoning in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) remains challenging because prescription decisions require integrating domain knowledge, syndrome differentiation, treatment principles, herbal prescription composition, and dosage determination. We develop a TCM language model family comprising models with 4 billion, 8 billion, and 14 billion parameters. The artificial intelligence contribution is a staged clinical alignment framework integrating large scale continued pretraining on TCM and clinical records, complementary reasoning supervision, and prescription-centered reinforcement learning (RL). We further formulate herbal prescription generation as a structured RL problem with prescription-level feedback, enabling direct optimization of clinical decision outputs beyond knowledge reproduction and generic instruction following. The engineering application is TCM clinical decision support, particularly herbal prescription recommendation. We evaluate the models on a public benchmark containing 25,620 expert-verified items across 13 TCM knowledge and clinical reasoning tasks and on a private retrospective dataset of 4,348 spleen and stomach disease prescription cases. The 14 billion parameter reinforcement aligned model achieves a prescription generation F1 of 37.0 on the public benchmark, compared with 32.3 for DeepSeek-R1 with 671 billion total parameters, and a herb-level F1 of 52.8 on the clinical dataset with improved dosage agreement. Reinforcement post-training consistently improves prescription recommendation across all scales, while physician-source analysis shows that expert heterogeneity affects reward stability. These findings demonstrate a scalable pathway from domain grounding and reasoning supervision to clinically oriented prescription decision support.

title: How to Build a Benchmark That Actually Measures Taste
shortTitle: How to Build a Benchmark That Actually Measures Taste
abstract: Expert-aligned "taste" benchmarks should reward craft judgment, not the ability to game the test. We introduce TasteBench, a pairwise good-vs-bad benchmark across visual, brand, book, and tech items under a frozen rubric with expert-only gold (panel n>=3; percent agreement >=0.60 primary gate; weak engagement labels train/analysis-only), together with a control protocol that separates craft judgment from test-gaming. Applying the protocol to a Round-1 pilot (primary_human_expert; three biological human experts; n=250 pairs) surfaces and quantifies three validity threats: two construction artifacts that inflate the trivial-baseline layer, and a difficulty ceiling that inflates every score. (1) Position: the preferred item is slot A with probability 0.956, so an always_item_a policy scores 0.956 (fair chance 0.5). (2) Lexical leakage: a filename token cue scores 0.912. (3) Difficulty ceiling: craft domains show near-ceiling human agreement (book/brand/tech 1.0), and even under A/B randomization (eval_assignment_seed7; gold_side_A ~0.47) all five VLM cards reach 1.0 on craft, with only visual separating (~0.84-0.91; a post-hoc hard subset, n=107, leaves craft at 1.0). The protocol (expert-only gold, a weak-label firewall, side randomization at construction, filename scrubbing, and hard filters) makes each artifact measurable and, for the two construction artifacts, correctable; we release a reference eval harness and a side-randomization tool, and show the tool removes the position skew (0.916 to 0.495/0.505). The result is a calibrated view of what the benchmark does and does not yet measure: position and leakage are fixable, whereas the craft-domain ceiling is a pair-difficulty limit that Round-2 must address. We do not evaluate engagement, era/circle conditioning, or calibration here, and we claim no general taste SOTA.

title: Vela: User Behavior as Supervision Sparks LLM Intelligence
shortTitle: Vela: User Behavior as Supervision Sparks LLM Intelligence
abstract: Large language models are increasingly deployed in applications that act on users' long-term behavior histories, from personal assistants to recommendation and advertising systems. These applications demand the user dimension of LLM intelligence: inferring a person's preferences, intent, and likely future actions from weeks to years of behavior data. Yet current models are trained on static text or synthetic data, neither of which captures how user behavior evolves over time. Real-world behavior records, already available at scale on content platforms and in personal-assistant agents, offer a natural supervisory signal. We propose user behavior as supervision and introduce Vela, a framework that converts real user behavior data into trainable tasks and trajectories. From the anonymized behavior records of 100,000 users, Vela generates 100,000 tasks across 91 real-world task templates; difficulty-based filtering and trajectory acceptance criteria retain approximately 75,000 tasks with selected training trajectories. Fine-tuning Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on these trajectories improves performance over the base model by up to 11.5 points on user-related tasks and by an average of 4 points on general benchmarks. Training on more user behavior data further improves user-related performance, and reinforcement learning after fine-tuning outperforms reinforcement learning from the base model by up to 7.7 points. These gains suggest that real-world user behavior is a scalable source of supervision for both user-centered capabilities and the broader intelligence of LLMs.

title: DeKoR: Decomposed Knowledge Routing for Efficient GNN--LLM Fusion
shortTitle: DeKoR: Decomposed Knowledge Routing for Efficient GNN--LLM Fusion
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown strong potential for text-attributed graph learning by leveraging rich pre-trained knowledge and language understanding capabilities. Combining LLMs with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) offers a promising paradigm for expanding the modeling capabilities of graph learning. However, LLMs and GNNs follow distinct learning paradigms, leading to a pronounced mismatch between their knowledge spaces. Such discrepancies make effective knowledge fusion nontrivial. Moreover, existing methods often incur substantial additional computation for only limited performance gains. To address these challenges, we propose DeKoR, an efficient framework for GNN and LLM knowledge fusion. To enable efficient knowledge transfer, DeKoR decomposes LLM knowledge into complementary local and global views and uses the LLM as an offline teacher to distill them into lightweight experts. To enable selective knowledge fusion, an adaptive router learns how much each node should rely on each expert. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate that DeKoR outperforms existing baselines on both node and subgraph classification, achieving superior effectiveness and efficiency.

title: PixARG: Pixel-Asynchronous Retrieval-Augmented Diffusion for Fast and Realistic Image Generation
shortTitle: PixARG: Pixel-Asynchronous Retrieval-Augmented Diffusion for Fast and Realistic Image Generation
abstract: While diffusion models achieve impressive image generation capabilities, they suffer from high computational costs, implausible artifacts, and limited adaptability to dynamic or private data due to static, centralized training. To address these, we propose PixARG, a novel retrieval-augmented generative framework that integrates dynamic real-world image retrieval into the diffusion pipeline to simultaneously enhance efficiency and visual realism. Specifically, PixARG constructs a pixel-level affinity map between the user's text prompt and the retrieved image to guide a heterogeneous noise initialization. By modulating noise intensity across spatial regions, this mechanism preserves semantically relevant structural priors while perturbing less relevant areas, thereby significantly accelerating convergence. To accommodate this spatially non-uniform noise and ensure synchronized generation, we introduce a pixel-wise asynchronous denoising scheduler and a spatiotemporal denoiser conditioned on the affinity map. Furthermore, we derive an affinity-adaptive training objective that elegantly balances deterministic restoration with stochastic regeneration across pixels. Experiments on LAION and COYO datasets across offline, online, and user-specific settings show PixARG enhances realism and semantic alignment while drastically reducing diffusion steps.

title: "Is Low Power Enough?" Rethinking Energy Efficiency in High-Fidelity Sensing
shortTitle: "Is Low Power Enough?" Rethinking Energy Efficiency in High-Fidelity Sensing
abstract: For two decades, long-lived sensor nodes have been built from the lowest-power parts, because their scalar readings take only milliseconds to acquire and send. Scientists now want higher fidelity data from the field, such as images and audio, and these observations break that rule: a low-power microcontroller stays awake for seconds to read, store, and transmit each one, so low power is no longer low energy. We argue that long-lived, high-fidelity nodes should instead be built around a more capable microcontroller, provided the whole board sleeps deeply. We revisit two principles from early sensor networks, "race to sleep" and "talk less", for high-fidelity data and on-device AI, and test them by comparing the STM32N6, which pairs a fast core with a neural accelerator, against the low-power Apollo4 Plus. Although the STM32N6 draws 1.9x more power, it completes an observation (capture, storage, on-board detection, and a LoRa transmission) 9.9x faster and so uses 5.2x less energy. On the same model, it runs inference with 3.2-11.4x less energy, and it fits models over 23 points more accurate. A high-fidelity node lives longest when it finishes quickly, sleeps deeply, and sends only what matters.

title: C2Flight: A Closed-Loop Co-Simulation Framework for Early-Stage Evaluation of Heterogeneous UAV Computing Systems
shortTitle: C2Flight: A Closed-Loop Co-Simulation Framework for Early-Stage Evaluation of Heterogeneous UAV Computing Systems
abstract: Early-stage design of heterogeneous UAV computing systems requires evaluating how algorithm, hardware, communication, and system topology affect closed-loop flight before the complete system is available. However, design choices interact through the robotic feedback loop, making task performance difficult to predict from isolated component metrics, while existing execution-driven approaches postpone system-level design feedback until the computing system is integrated. This work presents C2Flight, a closed-loop co-simulation framework that represents target systems as parameterized dataflow graphs and integrates models of hardware under design with independently accessible physical hardware through a unified node interface. Its graph runtime captures the combined effects of buffering, activation, resource sharing, communication, and local timing on closed-loop flight behavior. Validation against onboard and wireless offboard physical computing pipelines confirms its timing fidelity and closed-loop prediction accuracy. Two case studies demonstrate early-stage exploration of deployment and accelerator bit-width choices. These results show that C2Flight exposes system-level design trade-offs before full-system integration, enabling rapid early-stage design refinement.

title: CAG-WAM: Causal Action-Gain World Action Models for Robot Manipulation
shortTitle: CAG-WAM: Causal Action-Gain World Action Models for Robot Manipulation
abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) combine action generation with future prediction, allowing predicted futures to support action evaluation and robot decision making. However, the future associated with a candidate action may contain action-induced and environment-driven changes. Directly evaluating the predicted future may not fully characterize the future change associated with the candidate action. For example, a candidate action that worsens a favorable environmental future may still yield a favorable outcome, while one that improves an unfavorable environmental future may still yield an unfavorable outcome. To analyze this issue, we formulate a Structural Causal Model (SCM) for action evaluation in WAMs. The SCM formalizes how action-induced and environment-driven changes jointly shape future evaluation, and reveals a backdoor path through which environmental evolution can also affect the future evaluation associated with a candidate action. Intervention and backdoor adjustment account for this path, providing a causal basis for characterizing the future change associated with each candidate action. Based on this analysis, we propose Causal Action-Gain World Action Model (CAG-WAM). For each candidate action, CAG-WAM predicts an action-conditioned future and an environmental future under the same current observation, and defines their evaluation difference as causal action gain (CAG) for characterizing the future change associated with the candidate action. During training, we incorporate CAG into Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to guide robot policy learning. During inference, we evaluate the initial action with CAG and, when needed, revise it using predicted future information. Experiments on multiple benchmarks support the effectiveness of CAG-WAM.

title: Relational Semantic Grounding for Test-Time Discovery
shortTitle: Relational Semantic Grounding for Test-Time Discovery
abstract: Test-Time Discovery (TTD) aims to recognize known classes and detect novel ones from a continuous unlabeled test stream after deployment. Existing TTD methods mainly rely on visual clustering or prototype comparison, and can only assign anonymous labels to discovered classes, leaving them difficult to interpret in open-world applications. In this paper, we propose SEGA, a Semantic Grounding with Attributes framework for TTD. SEGA leverages large language models to generate attribute-rich descriptions for known classes and constructs an attribute-anchored visual-semantic space during training. At test time, we introduce Relational Semantic Grounding (RSG), which grounds unknown samples with similar and dissimilar known-class anchors, prompts the LLM to generate candidate concepts, and reranks them in the learned semantic space. The selected concept is further used for confidence-guided test-time semantic stabilization. By coupling attribute-level semantic alignment with relational concept grounding, SEGA transforms anonymous test-time clusters into interpretable semantic concepts. Experiments show that SEGA improves TTD baselines with the promise of semantic grounding for open-world.

title: Integrating AIRL-Based Reward Estimation into a Control Method Using Fuzzy Inference and Policy Gradient
shortTitle: Integrating AIRL-Based Reward Estimation into a Control Method Using Fuzzy Inference and Policy Gradient
abstract: A method integrating policy gradient with fuzzy inference has been proposed. This method, hereafter referred to as the base model, has high flexibility with respect to the configuration of fuzzy inference rules and fuzzy representation. It can also automatically adjust the rule weights and the membership functions in the antecedent and consequent parts using the same framework for learning. In methods that integrate reinforcement learning with fuzzy inference, however, the reward function must be designed in advance. It is therefore useful to add learning-based reward estimation to the base model. This paper proposes a fuzzy control method that integrates a reward estimation mechanism based on the adversarial inverse reinforcement learning (AIRL) framework into the base model. The generative adversarial nets (GAN) framework adopted in AIRL, however, tends to suffer from unstable learning. To address this, the proposed method treats the policy of the base model as the generator and also uses the set of membership functions in the policy as the cost function of the discriminator. This configuration allows the discriminator update for reward estimation and the generator update for policy estimation to be performed simultaneously on the parameters shared by both, without estimating a value function. In simulations of an illustrative vehicle speed control task, the proposed method acquired policies with high generalization performance through stable and efficient learning.
